issues.title: The November 3 ballot measures
issues.next: The Department of Elections certifies final local results by December 3, 2026.
issues.summary: San Francisco voters decided ten local measures (Props A to J) and a regional transit measure (RTM) on Nov 3. Six are charter amendments, including three placed by Mayor Lurie on how City departments, contracting and the ballot process work. Results are preliminary and will change as ballots are counted.
points: Charter amendments: A (changes affecting various City departments and commissions), B (a Municipal Finance Corporation and public bank), C (contributions to the Housing Fund), D (changes to the ballot measure process), E (City Administrator's authority and City contracting), F (executive branch management).

Ordinances: G (allowing private vehicles on the Great Highway in Sunset Dunes Park), H (a parcel tax to fund Muni operations), I (changes to the real property transfer tax), J (removing the foreclosure exemption from the transfer tax).
Regional: RTM, the Regional Transit Measure. On Sep 29 the Board consolidated that special election with Nov 3 (adopted unanimously).

Mission Local headlines on Nov 3 to 4 (preliminary): the BART and Muni measures were "winning with unexpected ease"; the public bank measure was "in tight race, but trending up"; one affordable housing measure was "set to pass, another unlikely to succeed."
The Department of Elections scheduled the first preliminary local results for 8:45 p.m. on Nov 3, with updates through the canvass.

How the Board placed its own measures: the public bank Charter amendment (Prop B) was ordered submitted 9-2 on July 7 (Sherrill and Wong opposed); a 13-part Charter amendment updating departments, boards and commissions 9-2 on July 14 (Chan and Fielder opposed); a Housing Trust Fund Charter amendment 11-0 on July 14; and the ordinance ending the transfer tax exemption for foreclosures (Prop J) 10-0 on July 28 (Walton excused).

attendanceNote: Counts cover the 10 regular Board meetings in this file with minutes, from Jun 30 to Oct 27, 2026 (the Board was on summer recess in August), not the full term. A member counts as present when recorded present at the meeting, even if excused partway through; mid-meeting excusals are noted on each meeting. Absences at roll call: Chen excused Oct 20; Melgar excused Oct 20. Minutes for the June 2, 9, 16 and 23 and Sept 15 and 22 meetings could not be opened, so those meetings are not counted.
